Ember

Ember is a from-scratch language model trained on one RTX 4090. Everything it knows was learned on that single card, under a fixed accounting contract: every trained token is receipted, every checkpoint is reproducible, and no result counts unless an artifact a third party can open says it happened.

The constraint is the experiment. One consumer card is a hard budget, so every question becomes a measurement question -- where the time actually goes, and what would have to change for it to go somewhere else.

As of2026-10-02T08:05:21Z· source events through2026-10-02T08:05:20Z

Current researchissue #1945

Training throughput on a single 4090

Make Ember's training step fast enough to apply 80,000 token positions per second on one RTX 4090 -- and prove it twice over: once across at least 1,024 warmed updates, and again across a continuous hour on the frozen production data mixture, without the model learning any worse than it does today.

Throughput is the budget for everything else. At today's rate a training run that would answer a research question takes long enough that the question changes first.

What remains for completion

3 of 6 conditions met — 3 remaining. Conditions are met or not met; this page states which, and computes no score over them. Being close on the measurement above does not partly satisfy anything.

  • REMAINING

    Speed, measured over at least 1,024 warmed updates

    At least 1,024 consecutive warmed updates sustaining more than 80,000 applied positions per second, by the tenth-percentile step.

    Unmet. The acceptance consumer measured a complete-update p10 of 58,499 over 74,884 updates on attempt 14; the threshold is 80,000.

  • REMAINING

    Speed, sustained for a continuous governed hour

    The same rate held for a full hour on the frozen production data mixture, not just over a burst of updates.

    Unmet. The governed hour on attempt 14 ran at 61,740 positions/s including checkpoint write and restore; the threshold is 80,000.

  • MET

    No worse learning

    An equivalence instrument licenses the fast number: whatever made it fast did not change what the model learns.

    Met on the current image-inclusive arm: the licence pair passed and the learned function matches.

  • REMAINING

    Protected evaluation minimum

    A protected benchmark suite runs against the checkpoint the qualifying hour produces, and clears its minimum.

    Unmet. The protected evaluation on the hour child is below its minimum, and real-image MMMU has not yet separated from the missing- and wrong-image controls.

  • MET

    Frozen production data mixture

    One admitted data identity -- shard ledger, receipt, tokenizer and cursor -- frozen so the hour binds to it and a later reader can reconstruct exactly what was trained on.

    Met. The amended image-inclusive mixture identity binds both trained-input digests.

  • MET

    One card, truthful accounting, receipts intact

    Everything runs on the single 4090, every governed run leaves a receipt, and every correction published stays published.

    Met. Owned, captured, restored, executor success, receipts intact.

Result in full
The frozen criterion reads: p10 below 25,400 applied positions/s REFUTES. The owned governor stopped the run at 104 accepted prefix rows (103 measured updates after the warm row) with a durable receipt whose order-statistic upper bound on the FINAL nearest-rank p10 over all 1,024 updates is 3,952.81 applied positions/s. That is a mathematical bound, not a projection: no completion of the remaining 921 updates could lift the p10 to 25,400. So the criterion is met by a factor of 6.4, and the campaign terminal of 80,000 by a factor of 20.2. K1-CAPTURED as implemented runs about 7x SLOWER than the standing governed 24,190.653, not 1.67x faster. There is NO governed 1,024-update number here: full_1024_rate is null and incomplete_1024 is true, so this arm does not join the count of the fifteen that carry one, and gate A does not move.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the defect is MINE. The census priced what K1 REMOVES and never priced what it ADDS. treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling's 2026-09-12 amendment says in as many words that a replacement's own cost is an unknown the selection owes as a MEASUREMENT, never inferred from the incumbent and NEVER ASSUMED TO BE ZERO -- and my 1.670x assumed exactly zero. The SRL controller's own runtime is absent from every line of that arithmetic: 16 decisions per update, a policy and value forward per 256-position segment, the H=8 rollout bookkeeping, and the per-site branching the captured-regions caller must perform before each Q/O or FFN product. Measured 3,952.81 upper bound against a 24,190.653 incumbent is a 7x REGRESSION, so the unpriced additions dominate the priced removals by roughly an order of magnitude. NOT CLOSED: (a) the 70.75 percent FLOP reduction itself, which is arithmetic from frozen dimensions and stands unrefuted -- what is refuted is that it reaches the timeline through THIS caller; (b) the K1 MECHANISM, since a caller whose branching cost is proportional to site count is not the only possible one and this measures one implementation; (c) K2, K3', J1 and J3, which the order file prices off this census -- their rows inherit the same unpriced-addition defect and must not quote 1.670x; (d) whether the controller cost is fixed per update or scales with sites, which decides whether any caller can recover the reduction and is one no-card measurement away.

(2) The assertion IS producible on this runner: L6-20260921T092627Z and L7-20260921T073649Z both carry capture.json with captured true and segments 13. The first REFUTED clause does not fire because K1 has no such assertion; the second does not fire because two of the mode-recording arms do carry it. Still open: (1) absence of an assertion is absence, never proof of eager execution; (2) capture.json presence, not execution_mode, is the discriminator -- two mode-recording arms carry no capture.json, so the campaign has three regimes on record (mode+assertion, mode-only, neither) and only the first is evidenced; (3) J2-CAPTURED and SRL8-4-CAPTURED carry the same null and the same missing assertion, so every arm I have named CAPTURED shares this defect and their numbers inherit it; (4) no step-time attribution here -- if K1 did run eager, how many of the ~7x milliseconds that accounts for is unmeasured; (5) the per-site branching cost inside the caller remains unpriced either way.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE IS READ FOR THIS CYCLE. UNIT is a GROUP keyed by (trace, kernel symbol, grid dimensions, block dimensions), so a symbol launched at two geometries is never compared against itself across them -- shape is excluded by the key rather than by hope. PREDICTOR is the DEVICE BUSY FRACTION over the 5,000 us immediately preceding each invocation's start, as a union of device intervals (kernel, gpu_memcpy, gpu_memset) clipped to that window divided by 5,000; the immediately preceding gap is NOT used, because clock and thermal state have a millisecond time constant and a microsecond gap cannot move it. SCORE per group is ordinary least squares of duration on busy fraction, read as the predicted duration at that group's OWN p90 busy over its predicted duration at its OWN p10 busy -- its observed span, never a fixed pair of thresholds. SCOREABILITY FLOOR, frozen: at least 200 invocations AND an interquartile range of at least 0.10 in busy fraction; a group whose predictor barely varies cannot score a slope in either direction and says so rather than passing vacuously. POOLED SCORE is the group scores weighted by group device time. VERDICT per arm: REFUTED (no load effect) if the pooled score is below 1.05; SUPPORTED at or above 1.05. SIGN CLAUSE, independent: at least two thirds of scoreable groups must share the sign of the pooled result, or the arm is INCONCLUSIVE because a 50/50 sign split is noise wearing a mean. COVERAGE FLOOR, independent: the arm is INCONCLUSIVE if fewer than three groups are scoreable or the scoreable groups carry below 0.30 of that arm's pooled device time -- the same floor the 2026-09-16 predecessor refused on, kept identical so the two are comparable. RESIDUAL is reported as a first-class number: the share of device time in unscoreable groups, with the reason each is unscoreable. BOTH ARMS are scored separately. If both clear their floors they must AGREE IN SIGN; a disagreement is reported as INCONCLUSIVE and as an instrument finding, never resolved by preferring one arm.

Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE INCONCLUSIVE DOES NOT CLOSE. It rules on the DESIGN, not on the load mechanism. NOT CLOSED: (1) the captured arm is unreachable by ANY within-trace design at this geometry -- at 0.8025 coverage the busy fraction varies by 0.004 to 0.010 on every large group, so the predictor has no spread and no regression can score it; reaching the dense arm needs a different predictor or a clock counter, not a better floor. Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTATION LEAVES STANDING, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING MEASURED TODAY. The reshape family is genuinely faster on the typical step: the launch configuration on top of the reshape beats the comparator by 2.0 percent at the median and 2.4 percent at p90, on a clean 1,024-update governed run, and reproduces its own summary quantiles exactly from the per-update series. The question this run cannot answer and the next one can: are the slow updates PERIODIC, and if so at what interval. A fixed stride points at something that fires every N updates -- a checkpoint or receipt write, an allocator release, an autotune recheck, a cache eviction -- and the rows already carry allocator bytes, cache eviction and transfer counters, staging seconds and routing digest seconds per update, so the mechanism is joinable to the slow set without any new instrumentation. If a named counter moves on exactly the slow updates, the mechanism is identified and the cure is bounded. If nothing moves on them, the dispersion is in the kernels themselves and the reshape family is simply noisier, which is a much worse answer and worth knowing before the freeze. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
The criterion is frozen on a join between the slowest decile of the launch-configuration-plus-reshape run and every numeric per-update counter its own rows carry, analysis-only, no card and no lease. Counters are taken as they appear in the rows rather than chosen after inspection, and the phase-seconds fields are EXCLUDED from the SUPPORTED decision because forward, backward and optimizer seconds are constitutive of a slow update rather than explanatory of it -- a slow update is slow in some phase by definition, and crediting that as a finding would be a gate comparing a value to its own source. SUPPORTED if at least one NON-PHASE counter has a slow-decile mean differing from the fast-nine-decile mean by a factor of at least 2.0 in either direction, or, for a counter whose fast-decile mean is zero, has a strictly positive slow-decile mean. A factor that large on a named counter identifies a mechanism. REFUTED if NO non-phase counter reaches that factor, which says the extra time is not accompanied by any recorded activity and the dispersion is inside the kernels. INCONCLUSIVE, explicitly and in advance, if a counter reaches the factor but is constant across the whole run, or varies but is identical in distribution between the two groups under inspection of its own values -- a factor computed on a near-zero denominator is arithmetic rather than evidence, and I would rather say so than report it. REFUTED, separately and on instrument grounds rather than on the hypothesis, if the slow set is not exactly 102 updates, or if the counters cannot be read for all 1,024 updates, or if the union of the slow set and the fast set is not the full 1,024 with no overlap. The residual clause: every key present in the rows must be classified as phase, non-phase numeric, or non-numeric, and the count of each is REPORTED, so a counter the join silently could not read shows up as a number rather than as a silence.

On slow updates the host forward time (0.1226) EXCEEDS the CUDA forward time (0.1086), meaning the host has stopped running ahead and is blocking inside the forward path. The dispersion that costs this run its p10 is a forward-path host stall, not a device-side cost, and backward and optimizer are untouched by it. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
The criterion is frozen on the per-update token delta, defined as cursor_after.token_offset minus cursor_before.token_offset, computed for all 1,024 captured updates of the launch-configuration-plus-reshape run, analysis-only, no card and no lease. SUPPORTED if the slow decile's mean token delta differs from the fast nine deciles' mean token delta by at least 20 percent in either direction. That is the threshold at which packing plausibly accounts for a 2.04x CUDA forward difference, and it is stated before the numbers are read. REFUTED if the two means differ by less than 5 percent, which says the slow updates consume essentially the same data as the fast ones and the extra forward time has no data-volume behind it -- making it a true stall. INCONCLUSIVE, explicitly and in advance, for the band between 5 and 20 percent, because a modest packing difference neither accounts for a 2.04x factor nor rules out a contribution, and choosing either reading on that evidence would be choosing the answer. REFUTED, separately and on instrument grounds rather than on the hypothesis, if either cursor field is missing or non-numeric on any update, if the deltas are not all non-negative, if the slow set is not exactly 102 updates, or if the recomputed p10, p50 and p90 of the run do not reproduce its own summary to within one part in ten thousand. The last clause is the identity check that the series read is the series the summary was computed from.

One update carries a delta of -4,190,208, the data cursor wrapping its shard, and the criterion refuses rather than letting me decide after the fact whether one row is discountable. The identity clause passed at 0.00e+00, the slow set is exactly 102, and no cursor field is missing, so the instrument is otherwise sound and only this clause fired.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and it is the answer arriving through the side door. The join reports exactly TWO distinct token deltas across all 1,024 updates: 4,096 and the single wrap. So document packing is CONSTANT, every update consumes identical data, and the slow decile is not doing more work because it was handed more data. The substantive hypothesis is therefore dead on this run's own numbers even though the criterion refuted on the wrap row, and a successor excluding that one row would rule REFUTED substantively rather than on instrument grounds -- worth stating so nobody re-runs it expecting a different answer. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE STALL. CUDA forward rises 2.0428x on the slow decile while the data is byte-for-byte the same volume, so the device genuinely executes more or slower work on identical input. That excludes a data explanation and leaves capture re-entry or a conditional fallback path as the live candidates, neither of which any recorded per-update counter would show. WHY THIS CYCLE IS NOT THE NEXT ONE. The operator's direction at 02:12 PM and again at 02:16 PM LA is the 80,000 terminal, and this stall is worth about five percent. The successor that matters is not this one: my own route arithmetic capped at 55,783 positions per second, and it held POSITIONS PER OPTIMIZER STEP fixed at 4,096 throughout while pricing only precision. That premise has never been measured. If device milliseconds per position fall as positions per step rise, the batch term and the precision term MULTIPLY, and the cap I published is an artifact of an unexamined constant rather than a property of the card.

SUPPORTED against the frozen criterion, both clauses, quoted. Clause one read: SUPPORTED if the summed fp16-with-fp16-accumulate time is at most 0.75x the summed bf16 time. Measured 1,488.17 us against 2,334.16 us over the model own seven dense site shapes, which is 0.6376x -- inside the line. So switching operands to fp16 buys 4.6 percent and switching the ACCUMULATOR buys the rest, which is the mechanism this cycle named and is the one that matters, because it means the lever is a compute-type flag over an fp16 operand pair and not a quantization scheme. THE COMPARISON AGAINST FP8 IS THE POINT AND IT IS DIRECT. FP8 measured 1.0134x under capture earlier today because its compiled quantize cost 149.06 us against a 41.76 us scaled GEMM -- a per-activation-byte tax against a per-FLOP saving. This arm pays no such tax: there is no amax, no scale and no cast kernel, and the 1.5685x is what the same card returns at the same shapes when the rate is reached without one. ONE SHAPE REGRESSES AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY. kv_proj, the narrow n=256 projection, is 0.739x -- SLOWER under fp16 accumulation, 24.8 us against 18.3. It is 18 us of a 2,334 us total so it does not move the sum, but a per-site dtype selection must exclude it rather than apply the flag globally, and a global flag would take that site backwards. THIS MEASURES DURATION ONLY AND LICENSES NOTHING. fp16 operands are a declared numerical treatment with a narrower dynamic range than bf16, which is a training-stability question this cycle does not touch; the no-worse-learning licence would need its own 64-update pair against the bf16 parent.
Limitations, and what this does not close
SUCCESSOR, and it is a governed arm rather than another probe: apply fp16 operands with fp16 accumulation at the CIADecoder dense projection funnel and measure 1,024 governed updates. The funnel already exists -- CIADecoder has zero nn.Linear and every dense projection goes through one _linear function, which was wired this afternoon for the FP8 arm behind an env flag and falls back to exactly F.linear when unselected. An fp16-accumulate arm is a strictly smaller change than the FP8 one that funnel was built for: cast the operand pair at the funnel and set the compute-type flag, with no quantize path, no scale, no weight cache and no autograd Function. The kv_proj exclusion is part of the arm, not a caveat: that site measured 0.739x and a global application would take it backwards, so the funnel selects per site by output width. THE STEP-LEVEL CEILING, with its premise stated separately from its arithmetic as a ceiling must be. PREMISE: the flag binds cuBLAS dense mm with fp16 operands and does not reach the Triton grouped-expert kernels, the flash attention backward, or any non-arithmetic kernel. Under that premise the affected population is the dense aten::mm class, 50.92 ms of the 154.83 ms governed device time, which at the measured 1.5685x becomes 32.46 ms for a step of 150.86 ms and 27,150 applied positions per second, 1.122x. Extending it to the grouped expert kernels, which are Triton and would need their accumulator changed in source rather than by a flag, reaches 1.183x; including the attention backward reaches 1.218x. Those are ceilings assuming perfect application and they are bounded below by nothing. WHAT THE FLOOR CHECK SAYS ABOUT 80,000, recorded here because it is the most useful thing this cycle produced and it is not a refutation. At the 240 TF/s these arms actually achieved, the unchanged 10.197 TF/step of arithmetic takes 42.5 ms. Add the measured 14.49 ms of non-device time and the step is 56.98 ms, which is 71,888 positions per second -- with EVERY non-arithmetic device kernel assumed removed or perfectly hidden. So the terminal sits just outside a perfect-everything floor at today achieved efficiency, and inside it if non-device time also falls: at 9.2 ms it is 79,245. The three conditions are therefore all live and all binding together, and the one this cycle did not move is condition B, efficiency against the rate, which stayed at 0.73 where 0.841 is needed.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING, AT ITS SOURCE. The verdict stands REFUTED on the frozen clause and does not move. The measured fixed share today is 0.1669 and the step is 164.33 ms. The campaign's own progress shrank both the step and the fixed fraction inside it, so the lever that amortises fixed cost got smaller as the step got faster. This is the standing law that an inherited factor must be repriced against the current measurement rather than carried, and it is the second lever in two days whose inherited price was wrong by more than a factor of two in the direction that made it attractive. WHAT THIS DECIDES FOR THE 80,000 TERMINAL, stated as arithmetic over the split above with its premise separate. 80,000 positions per second at 4,096 positions is a 51.2 ms step; the fixed terms alone are 27.42 ms, which is 53.6 percent of that entire budget. So at today's geometry forward and backward would have to fall from 136.91 ms to 23.78 ms, a factor of 5.76. Raising documents per step dilutes the fixed terms and lowers that requirement: at eight documents the required factor on forward and backward is 3.65, at sixteen it is 3.09, and in the limit it is 2.674. THE PREMISE, kept separate from the arithmetic: that forward and backward scale linearly with documents at a held sequence length of 1,024, and that the optimizer and host terms do not scale at all. The optimizer half is structural. The linearity half is an assumption that holds for adding documents and would NOT hold for lengthening them, since attention is quadratic in sequence length. SO THE TERMINAL'S REQUIREMENT IS NOW ONE NUMBER RATHER THAN THREE CONDITIONS: forward and backward device time must fall by a factor between 2.674 and 5.76 depending on documents per step, and every remaining route must act on that 136.91 ms. The contract lever is not a route to the terminal, but it is not worthless either -- it lowers the factor the real routes must deliver from 5.76 to 3.65 at eight documents, which is the difference between two levers stacking to enough and not. It remains a learning-contract change and therefore the operator's to rule; what has changed is that it is now correctly priced as an ENABLER of the arithmetic rather than as a route to the terminal, and it is not worth his attention on its own.
Limitations, and what this does not close
Ruled. The asymptote of positions per optimizer step is the variable-rate term, so geometry alone cannot reach the terminal. Not closed: positions per step is a LEARNING-CONTRACT change and remains the operator to rule, with its projected gain stated and never taken silently.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY RUN. The experiment is a LADDER of governed measurements at ONE head and one data plan, differing in exactly one field of geometry.json: documents_per_step in 4, 8, 16, 32, each at sequence_length 1024, warm_steps 1 and measured_steps 256. The 4-document rung is the MATCHED CONTROL and it runs in the same job, at the same head, on the same data, with the same statistic, because the single most expensive error on this campaign tonight was scoring arms against a comparator from a different head. Update COUNT is matched at 256 across rungs so the nearest-rank p10 is taken over populations of equal size; 256 is below gate A's 1,024, so NO number from this cycle is a gate A number and none is reported as one. CLAUSE 1, EXECUTION, decided first and from each rung's own receipt rather than from the geometry file it was handed. For every rung, applied_positions divided by measured_updates must equal documents_per_step times 1024 exactly. A geometry field is a REQUEST; the quotient is the EVENT. Any rung whose quotient does not match its request is INCONCLUSIVE for that rung and is never read as a result, because a rung that silently ran a different geometry has measured something else under this rung's name. CLAUSE 2, THE CONTROL IS LOAD-BEARING. If the 4-document rung does not execute and satisfy clause 1, the WHOLE cycle is INCONCLUSIVE regardless of what the other rungs return. A ratio against a comparator from another head or another job is exactly the defect being repaired. CLAUSE 3, REFUTED: clause 1 and clause 2 hold, and the highest executing rung's p10 is BELOW 1.15x the 4-document rung's p10. Below 1.15x the fixed per-invocation term is too small a share for geometry to act on the kernel-count row at all, and the lever is refuted as a way of reaching row 1 without authoring a fusion. CLAUSE 4, SUPPORTED: clause 1 and clause 2 hold, and the highest executing rung's p10 is AT OR ABOVE 1.24x the 4-document rung's p10 -- the low end of the asymptote range the mechanism predicts from the class table, taking the elementwise class as wholly scaling. CLAUSE 5, THE DISCRIMINATION FLOOR, frozen here so it cannot be chosen after the numbers are in: a ratio strictly between 1.15x and 1.24x is INCONCLUSIVE. No matched-run variation exists on any governed number in this campaign and every head's within-run p50-to-p10 gap is about 6 percent, so a ratio inside that band is not resolvable by one run per rung. That is a statement about this instrument, not a hedge against an unwelcome number. CLAUSE 6, RESOURCE REFUSAL IS A RESULT AND NOT AN INCONCLUSIVE. What the instrument own per-row output shows, and what the aggregate hid. That is 9314 us per step at 152 to 260 GB/s on a card whose DRAM rate is about 1008, with 864 of the launches carrying a non-contiguous operand. The launch counts match one launch per resident expert per weight matrix, so this is the expert weight-gradient accumulation path reading a transposed buffer. An elementwise add of the same elements is bit-identical whichever order memory is walked in, so a layout repair here is bit-exact and needs no licence pair. The successor is registered as a per-row cycle over exactly those four rows with a population that excludes graph-annotation joins by construction, and it is NOT this cycle re-run with a wider bound.

Limitations, and what this does not close
The successor is an INSTRUMENT REPAIR, not a treatment. The interval union is sensitive to where the profiler window lands and to every scheduling gap inside the step; per-window coverage in one reference arm ranged 0.8019 to 0.8986, which is a 10 point swing in what fraction of the window the union even covers. The successor hypothesis is therefore an ATTRIBUTION of the largest unexamined non-GEMM class, elementwise at 32,582.4 us/step, because it has no measured ceiling and nothing on the books has ever instrumented it. Criterion, frozen before the run

All three frozen clauses PASS. Null-pair spread 1.55 percent against a 15 percent ceiling. Rise 17.660 us per position against max(F=0.647, 1.80) = 1.800. Rise 17.660 against the half-predicted 2.650. The two-point fit puts the non-scaling population at 72333.4 us per optimizer step, 42 percent of the 170839.0 us step, against my predicted 21667. I under-predicted by 3.3x and the criterion cleared by 6.7x, so the verdict is not marginal -- and I record the OVERSHOOT as part of it, because a prediction wrong by 3.3x in the favourable direction is exactly the shape that deserves distrust rather than celebration.
Limitations, and what this does not close
THE CONFOUND, which the totals cannot resolve and which bounds every use of this result. Two different things produce a cost that fails to halve when positions halve. FIXED work is set by the parameter count or by the step itself and is collected by paying it less often. SUBLINEAR work is proportional in principle but runs inefficiently at the smaller size, and amortization collects NONE of it, because at depth N you run N full-size passes and pay the full-size cost each time. A two-point comparison of TOTALS cannot tell them apart, so 72333.4 us is an UPPER BOUND on the collectible population and must never be quoted as the lever size. Per class they do separate, and the class table is the real finding. Ratios of docs2 to docs4 cost: optimizer 1.078 and grouped_rows 0.919 are FIXED-like; gemm_dense 0.617, elementwise 0.667, grouped_weights 0.611, triton 0.675, other 0.606, gather 0.557 are scaling, though none reaches the ideal 0.5, so sublinearity is present everywhere. The optimizer at 1.078 is genuinely fixed and its 20964 us is collectible. The finding I did not expect is grouped_rows at 0.919: the grouped expert kernel costs almost the same for half the tokens, which is the signature of per-step EXPERT WEIGHT STREAMING whose bytes are set by the expert population rather than by token count. NOT CLOSED: whether grouped_rows is fixed or merely badly underutilised, which decides whether it is collectible at all and which needs a third point at docs=1 or 3 rather than another two-point fit. NOT CLOSED: the amortization ceiling itself. The proportional floor is 24.05 us per position, so perfect amortization of everything reaches 41580 positions per second and NO FURTHER -- 1.64x of today, the largest single lever measured on this campaign, and still not the terminal on its own. ALSO NOT CLOSED, and it changes which mechanism is right: gradient accumulation does not collect weight streaming, because each pass re-reads the weights. What collects it is more tokens sharing ONE weight read, and tokens per forward are capped at 4096 by a declared guard at ember_v0_residency.py line 713 and three sibling guards in ember_v0_decoder.py. Raising that constant is a context-length change to a canonical architecture and is not a throughput trick. The lawful shape is a BATCH dimension of independent 4096-position contexts, which multiplies tokens per weight read while changing no per-sequence semantics. That is the successor worth authoring, and it is large.

Measured p10 61,749.0 (p50 69,480, p90 72,782) with prefetch, against 70,009 p10 for threaded decode without it. Prefetch made it WORSE: cuda forward 11.2 -> 12.2 ms and backward 21.5 -> 24.8 ms median, consistent with 8 decode pool threads x 16 intra-op threads oversubscribing the 32 cores while the host issues eager work. Limitations, and what this does not close

Successor: trace the A1 step and attribute that idle to step start, eager segments, and context exit. Prefetch wiring is to be reverted; threaded decode kept.

Criterion, frozen before the run
fraction of answer-scoped captions exceeding 58 tokens is 0 (or negligible, <1%) AND the kept-tail question-stem-survival fraction is ~100% -- i.e. truncation essentially never bites in the actual manifest distribution, so the mechanism the counterpart seat found is real code but inert in practice
Instrument
CPU-only python script over the frozen combined-train-manifest.jsonl (sha ac0f6eb2...), no card, no protected MMMU items: (a) token-length distribution p50/p90/max + frac>58, (b) stem-survival vs options-only fraction for kept tails, (c) exact loss-bearing answer-letter token ids incl. leading whitespace, (d) one same-item parity: eval build_document vs training document via the 103619Z child, logits on letter tokens. Written to seat record: caption-truncation-census-20260928.json
Evidence
seat record: caption-truncation-census-20260928.json
Result in full
refuted-if required <1% over-cap AND ~100% stem survival; observed 68.97% of answer-scoped captions (121736/176518) exceed the 58-token cap, and of those over-cap rows only 0.013% (16/121736) retain any surviving stem token -- 99.99% are options-only. Truncation is not an edge case, it is the majority behavior.
Limitations, and what this does not close
AMENDED per this seat mail 38464 (methodological correction, arrived after mail 38465's report but before this update): the original stem_survives/options_only classification was a binary substring-match heuristic that presupposed a conclusion. Corrected measurement uses exact tokenizer per-token character offsets (Tokenizer.encode(...).offsets) to classify each over-cap row's question-stem retention as complete/partial/none, counts options fully retained, and checks whether the answer-letter's own option text survives -- broken down per dataset_id. Receipt: seat record: caption-truncation-census-20260928.json (schema v2). Frozen claim, reworded per this seat's instruction: truncation occurs at rate 68.97% (121736/176518 answer-scoped rows), with retention distribution: 0% of over-cap rows retain the COMPLETE question stem in any dataset; the majority retain it PARTIALLY (arxivqa 41.7% partial/58.3% none -- arxivqa is 77% of all rows and 97% of all over-cap rows; ai2d 77.5%/22.5%; scienceqa 75%/25%; m3exam-english 63.4%/36.6%; mmbench-dev-scienceqa 70.9%/29.1%). Options are mostly fully retained (82.6%-93.0% across datasets) and the answer-letter's own option text stays intact 82.6%-96.5% of the time. This is NOT "options-only" (the prior wording) and this census does not itself establish D-cause -- it establishes the truncation rate and retention shape only.

Criterion, frozen before the run
answer rows exceed 58 tokens (contrast real). Stop and re-rule if the first arm runs above 0.25 s per update. ## Frozen criterion (unchanged from 41515; pasted verbatim into loop predict before claim) - caption wrong-real (NLL wrong-image minus NLL real-image): REFUTED if the treatment does not exceed the control by 0.05 nats. - MMMU real-missing and real-wrong, n=847, no score bar. The statistic is the difference-in-differences: (treatment real-minus-contrast) minus (control real-minus-contrast). - Its interval is computed from PAIRED per-question outcomes, matched across every condition and both arms. It comes from a paired item bootstrap, resampling questions and never conditions independently. All per-question correctness vectors are saved in the receipt. - Exact method (the counterpart seat 42180): the interval is a 95% percentile interval over 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples of the 847 questions, seed 0. It is applied to control/treatment, and separately to the control/control null pair. The null pair is the INSTRUMENT CHECK, not an additive term. If its interval excludes 0, the run is REFUSED as non-discriminating before any verdict, and that check is applied before the treatment pair is read. - 0.0154, the one-score standard error, is NOT that interval. It is kept only as a preset OPERATING THRESHOLD: the treatment's statistic must exceed +0.0154 to count as a rise. (the counterpart seat 42166 correction, adopted before any predict.) - DECISION ORDER (amended 2026-10-01 02:06 AM LA on the counterpart seat 42760; mutually exclusive, first match wins; s = the statistic, [L,U] = its 95% interval): 1. Null-pair interval excludes 0 -> REFUSED (instrument does not discriminate; no verdict read). 2. U < 0 -> REFUTED-HARM (treatment worse than control). 3. s > +0.0154 and L > 0 -> SUPPORTED (a rise past the operating threshold). 4. s > +0.0154 and L <= 0 -> INCONCLUSIVE (point past the threshold, interval includes 0). 5. U < +0.0154 -> REFUTED (failed the preset bar; NOT evidence of harm). 6. Otherwise -> INCONCLUSIVE. Counterexamples: s=-0.002, [-0.010,0.005] -> rule 5 REFUTED. s=0.020, [-0.004,0.044] -> rule 4 INCONCLUSIVE. s=0.010, [-0.010,0.030] -> rule 6 INCONCLUSIVE. s=0.030, [0.006,0.054] -> rule 3 SUPPORTED. - Arm values (02:20 AM LA ruling WITHDRAWN 02:28 AM LA on the counterpart seat 42781: the carrier has no separate stem switch; the answer cap IS the treatment, so equal caps made the arms identical). Corrected, at carrier da91b549 (the counterpart seat source PASS 42781): CONTROL cap 58 (EMBER_ANSWER_CAPTION_TOKENS=58 set explicitly), TREATMENT cap 79 (the largest cap that fits 7 pairs: 7*(1+64+1+79+1)=1022 <= 1024); both arms 7 pairs per document (EMBER_PAIRS_PER_DOCUMENT=7; production is 8, so this is NOT production geometry) and image row start 149,664 in the seed-2163 order of manifest de32a445 (592,640 rows). 149,664 is the row OFFSET R: the first consumed row is (149,664 + 7*S) mod 592,640 with S the parent step, and the prep receipt binds S and that first row (the counterpart seat 42785). The null pair is control/control at cap 58. This is a CONTEXT-LENGTH observation: it does not prove the whole question survives. Loss-bearing targets per answer-scoped pair stay two (answer letter + end token) in both arms; the treatment adds conditioning tokens only (the counterpart seat 42785, image_text_stream.py 193-201). Before the card, the prep-only proof reports, for the actually selected answer rows, the count and fraction whose encoded length exceeds 58 (retained tokens differ between arms), and separately the full-fit fractions at 58 and 79.
